knowledge:
- key_parameters: method=The normalization method used (e.g., "MAS5.0", "GCRMA") which must match the classifier's requirements ;; targetValue=The target value for MAS5.0 normalization (e.g., 500), required if the input ExpressionSet has been subsetted or features are missing ;; allow.reweighted=Logical indicating whether to allow reweighting of probe-set weights if some probe-sets are missing from the input data ;; do.batchcorrection=Logical indicating whether to perform batch correction (defaults to TRUE, but can be set to FALSE if sample size is too small, though not recommended)
- alternatives: affy package=Used for initial normalization (MAS5.0 or GCRMA) of raw CEL files before importing into geneClassifiers
- when_to_use: When you have microarray gene expression data (specifically from platforms like Affymetrix HG-U133) and want to apply published disease classifiers (e.g., multiple myeloma risk classifiers like EMC92, UAMS70, HM19) to predict patient risk groups.
- pitfalls: Requires at least 20 samples (n >= 20) to accurately estimate means and standard deviations for batch correction; using fewer samples will trigger a warning and may yield invalid classifications ;; The normalization method of the input data must strictly match the classifier's required normalization method (e.g., MAS5.0 for EMC92, GCRMA for HM19) ;; Missing probe-sets will cause an error unless allow.reweighted = TRUE is specified, which alters the classifier weights and may result in different classifications ;; Input data must be unmanipulated output from normalization (not manually log-transformed or subsetted without specifying targetValue).

workflows.name: gene_classification
workflows.intent: Apply published gene expression classifiers to pre-normalized ExpressionSet data to obtain patient risk scores and classifications, with optional handling of missing probe-sets.
input: expression_set.RData (ExpressionSet object containing pre-normalized gene expression data)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and inspect available classifiers using showClassifierList and getClassifier ;; 2. Import and register the normalization method of the ExpressionSet using setNormalizationMethod ;; 3. Run the classifier on the normalized data using runClassifier (with optional allow.reweighted = TRUE if probe-sets are missing) ;; 4. Extract patient scores and risk classifications using getScores and getClassifications
workflows.code:
library(geneClassifiers)

showClassifierList()

EMC92Classifier<-getClassifier("EMC92")
EMC92Classifier

HM19Classifier<-getClassifier("HM19")
HM19Classifier

getWeights(EMC92Classifier)[1:10]

getDecisionBoundaries(HM19Classifier)

getEventChain(EMC92Classifier)

library(Biobase)
data(exampleMAS5)
class(exampleMAS5) #an object of class ExpressionSet
dim(exampleMAS5) 
preproc(experimentData(exampleMAS5))

fixedData <- setNormalizationMethod( exampleMAS5, method="MAS5.0", targetValue = 500 )
fixedData

resultsEMC92  <- runClassifier( "EMC92" , fixedData )
resultsUAMS70 <- runClassifier( "UAMS70", fixedData )

resultsEMC92
resultsUAMS70

data.frame(
    "score_EMC92"  = getScores( resultsEMC92 ),
    "class_EMC92"  = getClassifications( resultsEMC92 ),
    "score_UAMS70" = getScores( resultsUAMS70 ),
    "class_UAMS70" = getClassifications( resultsUAMS70 )
)

resultsEMC92.reWeighted <- runClassifier( 
    "EMC92" , 
    fixedData[1:70,] ,
    allow.reweighted=TRUE
)

resultsEMC92.reWeighted
